items.title: Xi Jinping meets Taiwan's KMT leader in Beijing

featured_image.name: On rare China visit, Taiwan's opposition leader calls for reconciliation

items.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping met Kuomintang Chairwoman Cheng Li-wun at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on Friday, marking the first meeting between a sitting KMT leader and China's Communist Party chief in nearly a decade. The encounter caps a week-long diplomatic push by Cheng, who has framed her six-day trip as a "journey for peace" aimed at easing military tensions across the Taiwan Strait.[1][2][3][4][5]

items.title: Study finds low oxygen can trigger limb regeneration in mice

featured_image.name: Scientists use stem cells to create synthetic mouse embryos

items.description: Salamanders and frog tadpoles can regrow entire limbs after amputation. Mammals cannot. A new study published April 8 in Science offers an explanation rooted not in genetics, but in how cells sense oxygen — and demonstrates that tweaking that response can awaken dormant regenerative programs in mouse tissue.[1][2]

items.title: Iran caps Hormuz transit at 15 ships a day under ceasefire

featured_image.name: Vessels pass through Strait of Hormuz following US-Iran ceasefire

items.description:
Iran will permit no more than 15 vessels per day to transit the Strait of Hormuz under the two-week ceasefire it agreed with the United States, a senior Iranian source told Russia's TASS news agency on Thursday. The cap, enforced under the supervision of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, represents barely a tenth of the roughly 130 ships that crossed the waterway daily before the conflict began on 28 February.[1][2][3][4]

"Under the current ceasefire, fewer than 15 ships per day are permitted to transit the Strait of Hormuz. This movement is strictly contingent upon Iran's approval and the enforcement of a specific protocol," the unnamed Iranian source said, adding: "There will be no return to the pre-war status quo."[4]

items.title: Ecuador doubles tariffs on Colombia to 100% as trade war deepens

featured_image.name: Ecuador raises tariffs on Colombia to 100% from 50% | The Star

items.description:
Ecuador announced on Thursday that it will raise tariffs on all imports from Colombia to 100 percent, effective May 1, in the latest and most dramatic escalation of a trade war between the two Andean neighbors that has been building since January.[1][2]

The government cited Colombia's "failure to implement concrete and effective border security measures" as justification for the increase, framing the levy as a sovereign response to drug trafficking along their shared border. "This measure is based on national security criteria and seeks to reinforce shared responsibility in a task that must be undertaken jointly to address the presence of drug trafficking at the border," the Ministry of Production, Foreign Trade, and Investment said in a statement.[2][1]

items.title: Russia and Ukraine agree to 32-hour Orthodox Easter ceasefire

featured_image.name: Putin announces Orthodox Easter ceasefire after rejecting Ukraine's proposal

items.description:
Russia and Ukraine have agreed to observe a 32-hour ceasefire over the Orthodox Easter weekend, with Russian President Vladimir Putin ordering his forces to halt combat operations "in all directions" starting Saturday, according to a Kremlin statement issued Thursday. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, who had been pushing for such a truce for more than a week, agreed to the pause.[1][2][3]

The ceasefire is set to begin at 4 p.m. Moscow time (1 p.m. GMT) on Saturday, April 11, and will last through the end of Easter Sunday, April 12. Defense Minister Andrei Belousov and Chief of the General Staff Valery Gerasimov have been instructed to halt all military operations during the period.[4][5][6][7]

items.title: MIT develops silent artificial muscle fibers for robots

items.description: Researchers at the MIT Media Lab and Politecnico di Bari in Italy have developed a new class of artificial muscle fibers that operate silently and without motors, external pumps, or bulky hydraulic equipment — a breakthrough that could reshape how robots move and how wearable assistive devices are built.

items.title: Trump says he's 'very optimistic' about Iran deal as Vance heads to Islamabad
items.description:
President Donald Trump said Thursday he was "very optimistic" about reaching a peace deal with Iran, even as a two-day-old ceasefire showed signs of strain over continued Israeli strikes in Lebanon and disputes about the status of the Strait of Hormuz.

In a telephone interview with NBC News, Trump said Iranian leaders were "much more reasonable" in private negotiations than in their public statements, but warned that "if they don't make a deal, it's going to be very painful."[1][2]
